function: Learned hybrid precoding for IRS-assisted mmWave MIMO-OFDM: cross-attention VAE denoises the channel, an autoencoder gives the analog precoder and a CNN the digital precoder (pp. 4-7).
system: IRS-assisted mmWave MIMO-OFDM: BS 32 or 64 antennas, user 16 or 32, reflecting IRS with 32 or 64 elements, 28 GHz, 2 GHz bandwidth, 128 subcarriers (pp. 3, 9).
method: Cross-attention VAE, autoencoder and CNN modules trained jointly on VAE (ELBO) and reconstruction (MSE) losses in an unsupervised manner; Adam, 200 epochs (pp. 5-8).
data_channel: MATLAB nrCDLChannel (3GPP TR 38.901 CDL) generates 60,500 samples: 45,000 training, 5,000 validation, 10,500 testing; system model text instead names Saleh-Valenzuela (pp. 3, 7-8).
test_conditions: Same-distribution train/validation/test split; SNR sweep -10 to 20 dB; results for (Nt,Nr)=(32,16) and (64,32), L=1,2,3, and 10-30% added noise; retraining per case not stated (pp. 8-13).
baselines: Learned: Sparse-MATT-DAE and DAE-CNN-ATT (authors' earlier models), SPR-CNN, Cv-DnCNN, LSTM; non-learned: SCA precoding in place of AE+CNN, in the proposed pipeline (pp. 8-12).
metrics: MSE and achievable rate versus SNR, EVM, SINR, average precoding gain; sweeps over antennas, paths and added noise (pp. 7-13).
complexity: Table II: big-O complexity of the proposed model and five baselines in Nt, Nr, d_i and layer sizes; inference time 0.37 s versus 0.34-0.43 s for three baselines (pp. 7-8).
q1_support: p. 7: "We generate our data using the nrCDLChannel package in MATLAB"; p. 8: "Technical Report TR 38.901, facilitating the simulation of realistic wireless environments". Training, validation and test sets all come from this generator (p. 8).
q2_support: p. 8: "By maintaining the same data distribution across all sets"; p. 13: "We assess robustness through modified propagation paths and noise experiments". The paper does not state which conditions were used for training in the L, antenna and noise experiments, so no unseen condition is established.
q3_support: p. 8: "SPR-CNN-Precoding: Employs convolutional neural networks (CNNs)"; p. 9: "LSTM-Precoding: Uses an LSTM model similar"; p. 11: "We compare three different precoding combinations" including SCA; p. 12: "SCA is a traditional nonlinear problem optimization method".
q4_support: p. 7: "Table II compares the computational complexity" and inference times of "0.37, 0.43, 0.38, and 0.34 seconds" for the proposed model and three baselines; the big-O expressions are in Table II (p. 8).
q5_support: p. 7: "We generate our data using the nrCDLChannel package in MATLAB". The data come from a MATLAB generator; the paper gives no code or data link and uses no public dataset.
notes: Area 3 because the stated goal is precoding design maximizing the achievable rate (p. 5, Eqs. 8a-8c) and the modules output the analog and digital precoders; the channel-denoising module and the MSE metric make area 2 a possible alternative. The IRS phases Theta are an input of Algorithm 1 (p. 6), not learned. q3 is a flagged call: the non-learned comparison is the SCA variant of Fig. 9 (SCA replaces the AE+CNN precoding modules while the VAE front end is kept), and Figs. 4-7 compare only learned methods; if SCA is not accepted as a non-learned baseline, q3 is 0. q1 relies on the nrCDLChannel statement (pp. 7-8), although p. 3 says the channel model is Saleh-Valenzuela, Table III lists 4 paths while the text uses L=1,2,3, and p. 8 gives 60,500 samples in one place and 50,000 in another. Tables II and III were read from the page images (pp. 8-9).
